title: Fix Stale Window Engagement Overlay Padding Test
description: The Shell components test "Window anchors engagement in a top overlay when active" in ui/js/react/index.tsx asserts `overlay?.className` contains "p-single", but `windowEngagementOverlayClass` ends in `p-0`. Determine whether the test assertion is stale (padding utility intentionally removed) or the class regressed (padding was dropped and should be restored), then fix the actual mismatch. Also check `utilityBarOverlayClass` (identical trailing `p-0`) and `windowSearchOverlayClass` (identical trailing `p-0`) for the same staleness, and search for any other `p-single`/`p-0` test assertions on these overlay classes that need reconciling.
summary: Root-caused the stale test: commit e1ce6138 (2026-07-13, "264") intentionally changed windowEngagementOverlayClass, windowMeasuresOverlayClass, windowToolbarOverlayClass (now utilityBarOverlayClass) from `p-single` to `p-0` to avoid a double edge-gap against the window frame inset, and added a dedicated regression test ("Window panel overlays use the window frame inset...") asserting `p-0` and NOT `p-single` for all of them. The older test "Window anchors engagement in a top overlay when active" was never updated and still asserted `p-single`, so it was silently failing (masked by the separate full-suite OOM issue). Checked utilityBarOverlayClass and windowSearchOverlayClass and the canonical p-0 test already covers both correctly — no other stale p-single/p-0 assertions found nearby. Fixed the outdated assertion at ui/js/react/index.tsx to expect `p-0`, matching the intentional implementation. Verified both the fixed test and the canonical p-0 regression test pass via `bun ./script.ts test -t "..."`.
